entries.title: Carry explicit context through safe structured logs
entries.summary: Carry validated correlation separately from verified authority, project safe events, and prove request/job isolation and terminal outcomes.
entries.body:
## Use when

A request crosses services or becomes a background job and its outcome must be diagnosable without exposing its inputs. Reuse the application's existing context and logging owners.

## Keep the boundary small

Validate or generate a bounded correlation ID at ingress. Obtain the actor and scope from the real authentication/authorization owner, separately from caller metadata. Pass an immutable context explicitly, or use the runtime's existing scoped context with guaranteed restoration. A matching ID or schema never grants authority.

Project a small event before serialization: operation, terminal outcome, elapsed time and approved correlation fields. Exclude whole requests, URLs, credentials, payloads and arbitrary exceptions. Redaction is additional protection. Record mutation success after the transaction returns successfully. A service outcome and an HTTP stream outcome are distinct observations; the HTTP owner must handle finish/error/disconnect races once.

## Portable example

Save as example.py and run with Python 3.11+. Only standard-library modules are required; see [asyncio tasks and cancellation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html) for the concurrency API used below. The save callback represents authorized work and must return after its owned commit. This demonstrates explicit propagation and event projection; it is not an authentication system, durable queue or HTTP disconnect handler.

~~~python
import asyncio
import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from time import perf_counter
from uuid import uuid4

lines: list[str] = []  # Capture sink; use the existing logger in an application.


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Context:
    request_id: str
    actor: str


def context(candidate: object, verified_actor: str) -> Context:
    valid = isinstance(candidate, str) and re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}", candidate)
    return Context(candidate if valid else str(uuid4()), verified_actor)


def emit(ctx: Context, outcome: str, started: float) -> None:
    if outcome not in {"ok", "failed", "aborted"}:
        raise ValueError("unknown outcome")
    lines.append(json.dumps({
        "operation": "export",
        "outcome": outcome,
        "request_id": ctx.request_id,
        "duration_ms": round((perf_counter() - started) * 1000),
    }))


async def export(ctx, save):
    started = perf_counter()
    try:
        await save(ctx.actor)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        emit(ctx, "aborted", started)
        raise
    except Exception:
        emit(ctx, "failed", started)
        raise
    emit(ctx, "ok", started)


async def request(headers, verified_actor, save):
    ctx = context(headers.get("x-request-id"), verified_actor)
    await export(ctx, save)
    return {"request_id": ctx.request_id}


async def job(metadata, current_authorized_actor, save):
    # The job owner rechecks current authority; never restore an actor from metadata.
    await export(context(metadata.get("request_id"), current_authorized_actor), save)


async def demo():
    actors = []

    async def save(actor):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)  # Yield to expose accidental shared-context use.
        actors.append(actor)

    first, _ = await asyncio.gather(
        request({"x-request-id": "r-a", "authorization": "PRIVATE"}, "actor-a", save),
        request({"x-request-id": "r-b"}, "actor-b", save),
    )
    await job(first, "current-worker-actor", save)
    assert actors == ["actor-a", "actor-b", "current-worker-actor"]
    assert [json.loads(line)["request_id"] for line in lines] == ["r-a", "r-b", "r-a"]
    assert "PRIVATE" not in "".join(lines)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(demo())
~~~

Capture the actual serialized sink. Add a failing callback and a cancelled task: each must emit one failed/aborted event, propagate the exception and emit no success. Run overlapping requests and a job under a different current actor. If using Python ContextVar instead of explicit arguments, bind with token = variable.set(value) and reset(token) in finally at the same owner; test restoration after both exceptions and cancellation.

## Adaptation and limits

No logging library is mandatory. In an existing Pino application, CFOBooth's createSafeLogger constructs Pino and projects declared fields in record(ctx, event) before writing. Its executeServiceOperation wraps the awaited capability outcome. Reuse those owners there. Its issuer WeakSets and expiring job authorities are local security mechanisms, not portable credentials. The standards still describe background authority as future work, while the inspected schedule issuer/recheck already implements a narrow form; do not copy that older statement as current behavior.

FlowFilliates' canonical backend guide requires named Logger instances in its NestJS application; its older logging.md says the opposite and permits error payloads. Preserve its deliberate naming choice when working there; do not adopt arbitrary error serialization as this recipe.

StackOS provides a useful counterexample: RequestIdMiddleware sets/resets a request ContextVar, but the inspected log injector reads different run/project variables with no production bind sites found. The middleware comment claims more than that wiring proves. This is partial propagation, not an end-to-end exemplar. Clickgram's logger comment says production JSON, while its selected console formatter uses printf; emitted JSON was not verified.

## Source snapshots

These are inspected implementation and authored-test evidence, not source-project test passes.

Authored tests: libs/server-core/src/lib/context.spec.ts:113–181; libs/observability/src/observability.spec.ts:250–283; libs/server-core/src/lib/http.spec.ts:206–267.

- StackOS@57f97cbbc9b48a9bb298f568cbc44a1c81fd59fe: stackos/api/errors.py:73–98 and stackos/logging.py:102–114 (partial implementation).
- Clickgram@39cefc9a0488af6f32dcfbfba1e82a9f65f319e4: services/admin-api/src/config/logger.config.ts:6–48 (comment/config conflict).

entries.title: Keep one capability owner behind every transport
entries.summary: Route transports through one capability and persistence boundary with explicit transaction ownership and proportionate proof.

entries.title: Share boundary contracts and keep private types local
entries.summary: Share contracts across real consumers, derive variants, validate unknown inputs and keep implementation types local.

entries.title: Make agent guidance a linked ownership map
entries.summary: Use root and module guides to route maintainers to canonical owners, affected consumers and focused proof.
entries.body:
## Use when

An unfamiliar maintainer or agent needs to find a capability's owner, contracts, callers and proof. Root guidance should route; module guidance should expose the local responsibility and the neighbors that can break.

Keep product authority and shared rules at their canonical source. Link to them instead of copying a whole manual into each directory. Scoped guides refine applicable parent rules; actual automatic discovery and precedence depend on the chosen host, so follow its contract and explicitly read required links. A filename alone does not enforce policy.

## Portable directory and guide examples

This is an illustrative repository map, not files to scaffold automatically. The named implementation/docs/tests are the existing owners in this example.

~~~text
AGENTS.md
docs/architecture.md
docs/verification.md
src/api/AGENTS.md
src/reports/AGENTS.md
src/reports/service.py
src/reports/repository.py
tests/test_reports.py
~~~

Root AGENTS.md:

~~~markdown
# Project guide

Read [architecture](docs/architecture.md) for product boundaries and
[verification](docs/verification.md) for proof commands.

| Change | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| Report policy or persistence | [Reports](src/reports/AGENTS.md) |
| HTTP input, auth or response mapping | [API](src/api/AGENTS.md) |

Before editing, trace the actual producer and affected consumers.
Update affected contracts, callers and proof together.
~~~

src/reports/AGENTS.md:

~~~markdown
# Reports

Read with the [root guide](../../AGENTS.md),
[architecture](../../docs/architecture.md), and [API owner](../api/AGENTS.md).

- [service.py](service.py) owns report authorization and transaction completion.
- [repository.py](repository.py) owns report SQL using that transaction.
- API and job callers delegate to the service; neither recreates its policy.
- A denied actor cannot create a row. Publish success only after commit.
- Keep private row-mapping types here; shared wire shapes follow architecture.

Review affected API/job callers after changing service inputs or outcomes.
Run the report checks in [test_reports.py](../../tests/test_reports.py)
using the command selected by [verification](../../docs/verification.md).
Update this map when ownership, consumers or proof obligations change.
~~~

Read the root, follow Reports, inspect the service and repository, then follow the API link and the report test. A maintainer can now identify the owner, affected callers and required proof without searching unrelated modules. Confirm the files and links actually resolve; inspect calls and tests before asserting that the map is accurate. The Markdown example proves routing, not implementation correctness.

## Maintenance and tradeoffs

Add a deeper guide when a real ownership boundary needs it. Prefer a short invariant and impact-review link over a growing list of incidents, pixel adjustments or copied release notes. Detailed operational/design contracts can stay in their existing dedicated documents.

When structure changes, update links and the affected guide in the same change. If documentation and code disagree, record both: code establishes current behavior, while approved product requirements still establish intended behavior. Investigate the discrepancy instead of silently treating implementation as permission to narrow the requirement.

Do not create a second tracker, policy engine or documentation framework. Keep run-specific state and temporary evidence in the existing task/run owner; keep reusable navigation in guidance.

## Source snapshots

These are inspected guidance and implementation-navigation examples, not executed source-project tests.

- StackOS@57f97cbbc9b48a9bb298f568cbc44a1c81fd59fe: AGENTS.md:10–47 and docs/README.md:1–53 (root/router); ui/AGENTS.md:1–37 and stackos/repositories/AGENTS.md:1–48 (scoped ownership maps). The repository guide's transaction-helper rule can be followed to the existing persistence owner; the UI guide separates feature-local types from shared consumers.
- CFOBooth@6a663eb1ef4da35c1fd1a562722d64e85fd62794: AGENTS.md:34–55 (root/module navigation); libs/contracts/AGENTS.md:5–34 and libs/repositories/AGENTS.md:5–31 (concrete seams and impact review). apps/ui/app/components/widgets/AGENTS.md:3–17 links parent, selected design, implementation and proof.
- FlowFilliates@9974c29dc93c27d8afd308976160ae7b134b1907: AGENTS.md:35–70 (routing/short invariant guidance); apps/admin-api/src/features/agent-api/AGENTS.md:3–26 (scope and required adjacent-owner review).

CFOBooth and FlowFilliates also contain long amendments despite their concise-guide rule. The transferable recommendation is the linked ownership map, not their file length, domain policies or host-specific tooling.
